newsitem.title: USA: Union says deadline nears in Chino labor talks.
newsitem.headline: Union says deadline nears in Chino labor talks.

text.p: The union negotiating with Phelps Dodge Corp at the company's Chino copper mine in New Mexico said it will take unspecified action unless it receives further information from management.
"If I don't get anything within the time frame the attorneys and I have established, then we will take other action," United Steelworkers of America's lead negotiator at Chino, Robert Guadiana said.
He declined to say what the action would be or disclose a deadline. "But it's not too far away," Guadiana said.
Phelps officials were not immediately available for comment.
Phelps told the Steelworkers Union that Chino workers were among the highest paid in the industry, Guadiana said.
The union then requested information about rates of pay and benefits at non-unionised copper facilities to verify Phelps' view.

The company said it was unable to give this information, but the union replied it must, Guadiana said. The union requested this data again more than three weeks ago and is waiting for a reply, he added.
Workers at Chino have been without a labor contract since June 30 last year. Talks between the union and management have stalled several times.
Guadiana said Chino was operating at about 70 percent of its 169,000 tons per year capacity because of disgruntlement among workers.
However, Phelps has repeatedly said Chino is operating normally.
The company said last August it made what it termed its final offer, a four year pay freeze.
